name: Vespers
introduction: We pray the Eleventh Hour commemorating the taking down of our Lord from the Cross and His burial.
psalmsIntro: From the Psalms of our father David the prophet and king, may his blessings be upon us all. Amen.

sections.title: The Beginning of the Vespers Prayer
content: The praise of the blessed Vespers, I offer to Christ my King and my God, beseeching Him to forgive me my sins.

sections.rubric: Glory to You, O our God. Holy, holy, holy. A reading from the Gospel according to our teacher Saint Luke the Evangelist. May his blessings be with us all. Amen.

content: We worship You, O Christ, with Your Good Father and the Holy Spirit, for You have come and saved us. Lord have mercy.
O Lord, Who at the Eleventh Hour was taken down from the Cross: take away our sins from us. Lord have mercy.
We have sinned and committed iniquity, we have acted wickedly; have mercy upon us and forgive us. Lord have mercy.
O Lord, as the sun sets and the daylight fades, we praise and glorify You, for You have brought us to the evening time. Lord have mercy.

sections.title: Absolution
content: We thank You, our compassionate king, for You have granted us to pass this day in peace, and brought us to the evening thankfully, and made us worthy to behold daylight until evening. Lord, accept our glorification which is offered now, and save us from the trickeries of the adversary, and abolish all the snares which are set against us. Grant us, in this coming night, peace without pain, or anxiety, or unrest, or illusion; so that we may pass it in peace and chastity, and rise up for praises and prayers. And thus, at all times and everywhere, we glorify Your holy name, together with the Father, who is incomprehensible and without beginning, and the Holy Spirit, the Life-Giver, Who is in one essence with You, now and at all times, and unto the ages of all ages. Amen.
